title: Turkey, light meat, roasted, skin eaten

content.title: About
content.content: Turkey is a large bird native to North America. Light turkey meat roasted with the skin on has a mild flavor, moderately dry texture, and a subtle aroma. The skin, cooked until crisp, is edible and adds extra flavor and healthy fats.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Turkeys were domesticated by Native Americans over 2,000 years ago.
Light turkey meat contains less fat than dark meat, but the skin retains some beneficial fats.
Roasting with the skin helps retain moisture, keeping the meat juicier.
In the United States, turkey is strongly associated with Thanksgiving.
Edible turkey skin is rich in collagen, which is beneficial for skin and joints.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Light turkey meat is an excellent source of high‑quality protein needed for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Compared with red meat, turkey contains less saturated fat, making it a heart‑friendlier option.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Turkey provides niacin (B3) and vitamin B6, which support metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: It supplies selenium, zinc, and phosphorus, important for immunity, bone health, and antioxidant protection.

items.title: Collagen in the skin
items.content: Crispy turkey skin contains collagen that may help maintain skin elasticity and joint health.

items.title: Poultry allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to turkey meat or skin.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Roasting often involves added salt; excess sodium can be problematic for people with hypertension.

items.title: Possible bacteria
items.content: Undercooked turkey can harbor Salmonella or Campylobacter; ensure it reaches an internal temperature of 74 °C.

items.title: Cholesterol in the skin
items.content: The skin is higher in cholesterol; those with elevated cholesterol should consume it in moderation.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Sliced roasted turkey with skin can be served as a main dish, added to salads, sandwiches, or incorporated into hot meals. The crisp skin can be eaten as a snack, seasoned with herbs or spices.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked turkey in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze in a freezer‑grade bag for 2‑3 months. Reheat to an internal temperature of 74 °C before serving.
